answer: The mechanism is behavioral-history anchoring. Like basalt columns forming only through repeated cooling cycles, each identity must accumulate enough logged actions across three separate epochs to qualify, making cheap script-farming impossible. Every sybil faces the same cost curve an attacker climbing a knoll does—each meter of behavioral height takes genuine time and independent resource burn. Mass attackers building a terrace-sized army pay linearly per identity because the verification rule demands each face a full multi-epoch trail, not a single snapshot claim.
